functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Transitional muscle at the boundary of the anterior (femoral n.) and medial (obturator n.) thigh compartments -- documented dual innervation reflecting this position, forms the floor of the femoral triangle.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

trigger_points.location_description: Muscle belly within the femoral triangle, deep and difficult to palpate directly
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: A well-localized, strong zone (roughly 8-12 cm) of deep aching/sharp groin pain within the femoral triangle, with more diffuse radiation toward the anteromedial thigh; occasionally felt in the hip joint itself
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Falls with the legs splayed, hip or gynecologic surgery, and excessive adductor-group tension; less often activated by an arthritic hip
trigger_points.notes: A 2026 case report documented pectineus myofascial pain syndrome presenting as chronic, cough-provoked groin pain that mimicked an inguinal hernia and resolved with ultrasound-guided dry needling, underscoring that not all cough-induced groin pain is hernia-related
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual (Travell JG, Simons DG, Simons LS, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 2: The Lower Extremities, 1st ed., Williams & Wilkins, 1992; Donnelly JM, Fernandez-de-las-Penas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds), 3rd ed., Wolters Kluwer, 2019) -- as cited in direct peer-reviewed case report: Yildirim S, Ayyildiz A, Temel MH, Bagcier F, Coskun E (2026) 'Cough-Induced Groin Pain: Misleading Symptom or Diagnostic Key for Differential Diagnosis.' Clin Med Insights Arthritis Musculoskelet Disord 19:11795441261417711, doi:10.1177/11795441261417711 (https://doi.org/10.1177/11795441261417711) -- retrieved via PubMed; and clinical description of the femoral-triangle pectineus referral zone in the trigger-point literature
